story.title: Binance CEO says 90 percent of stolen assets have been ‘replenished’

facts.text: Binance says it has replaced 90% of $6.3 billion stolen in record crypto hack
The incident has sent shockwaves through the cryptocurrency industry.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin cuts some losses, but falls below $77k after Binance hit with $6.3B hack
The latest update marks progress from the exchange's previous disclosure that it had covered approximately 80% of the stolen assets.
Binance said the remaining tokens were less liquid, making them more difficult to source and replace.
In a social media update, Binance said it had been replenishing affected assets, including Bitcoin, Zcash and stablecoins USDT and USDC.
The replacement funds have come from a combination of the company's treasury, emergency reserves and insurance funds.
The exchange also said it was working to restore withdrawals by Sunday.
Binance's commitment to make users whole and its plan to resume withdrawals are key steps in its effort to restore confidence following the attack.

After hackers stole a shocking $6.3 billion from Binance customers in a record-breaking crypto heist, the company’s CEO says that 90 percent of the funds have been replaced, and the company plans to cover the remaining 10 percent as well.

Two days after analysts said North Korean hackers likely executed a brazen $6.3 billion crypto heist on the blockchain platform Binance, the company says it has replenished about $5.7 billion in the stolen assets.
In an update on Saturday morning, Binance said it tapped its corporate treasury to purchase billions of dollars in crypto from the market and private brokers.

"Our users will not bear the financial impact of this incident." Binance already had an emergency fund of about $1 billion for situations like this, but the unprecedented scale of the attack rendered that piggy bank insufficient to cover the losses.
In 2025, the FBI named the same group responsible for a $1.5 billion hack on Bybit, another crypto exchange.
On Thursday, around 4 p.m., Binance reported a security breach on its blockchain network that it initially said was made possible by a compromised employee laptop.
To remediate the heist, Binance also tapped into its Futures Insurance Fund, a regulatory requirement typically used to protect traders against losses suffered during extreme market conditions.

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from a $6.3 billion security breach, with around 90% of the stolen token assets already replenished.
The exchange said it is working to restore withdrawal services in phases.
Binance said Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), Tether (USDT), BNB, Solana (SOL), USD Coin (USDC), XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC were fully backed.
It would continue buying the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter (OTC) channels until coverage reached 100% for all tokens.
Binance also announced plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves report by Monday, November 2, allowing users to verify the digital assets backing their account balances.

Binance has not publicly confirmed who was responsible for the attack and said its investigation remains ongoing.
"That covered amount is now up to 90%," it added.
